articles.title: Biopsies, aerial drills and a personal pizza: a day in the life of a shark scientist
articles.summary: Jasmin Graham, a shark scientist and science communicator, also makes time in her day to practice her hobbies and play music bingo with friends. “Sharks are not monsters, they just need better PR,” writes Jasmin Graham. And she should know: Graham is a shark scientist and science communicator.
body: Here’s what a day in Graham’s life in Sarasota, Florida looks like.
I usually wake up around 8am, but I woke up at 7am because I had to go to the dentist. I got a head start on some emails and took a fundraising phone call in the car.
After the dentist, I got home and did my drills. I’m an aerialist, which is basically all the things you see in Cirque du Soleil: lyra [aerial hoop], pole and silks. Breakfast was Honey Nut Cheerios.

I went to the office to meet with an artist in residence [with Graham’s nonprofit Minorities in Shark Sciences ]. They’re helping build props and sets for our theater shows. One is an immersive experience about the mass extinction of sharks. It’s a combination of a whodunit and an escape room.
points: Jasmin Graham, a shark scientist and science communicator, also makes time in her day to practice her hobbies and play music bingo with friends.

articles.title: Kindness of strangers: A hall-of-fame athlete helped my 94-year-old mum buy a vacuum cleaner
articles.summary: A woman in the queue said she was happy to drive an hour, pick up the vacuum, then bring it to Mum’s house. I was worried – but how wrong I was! For a 94-year-old woman, my mother is still very busy and active.
body: Unfortunately, the shop in her area had sold out by the time she got there. The sales assistant told her it was still available in another Melbourne store – but that store was an hour’s drive away. As active as she is, Mum pointed out that at her age, she really could not manage a drive of that length. She asked the sales assistant if they could transfer the vacuum to this store and was flatly told no.

Just as Mum was feeling a bit taken aback by the poor customer service, the woman in the queue behind her interjected. She told Mum that she was happy to drive all that way, pick up the vacuum, then bring it to Mum’s house for her.
The woman in the queue seemed to be a genuinely nice person, so Mum allowed the vacuum to be ordered for her and gave the woman her address.
As Mum recounted this story to me later, my heart sank. I couldn’t envisage a good outcome. But how wrong I was!

articles.title: Phoebe Bridgers and Her Leg Hair Make for a Memorable Venice Film Festival Debut
articles.summary: For a turn around the Lido, musician and “Primetime” actor Phoebe Bridgers embraced the glamorous yet free-spirited Venice dress codes her way.
body: Yesterday, Phoebe Bridgers made her debut at the Venice Film Festival, where her first turn as an actor in A24’s Primetime was received with an enthusiastic seven-minute standing ovation and chants of “Phoebe! Phoebe!” The musician also brought a more unexpected detail to the Lido.

The singer arrived at the film’s photocall in a sharply tailored black skirt suit from Gucci’s fall 2026 collection. She accessorized with Gucci oval-frame sunglasses, Stuart Weitzman Babette pumps, and a chunky Leo Black Grandfather silver signet ring. With this sleek, controlled silhouette, her hair swept back and makeup kept soft and barely there, it’s a look that revels in the elegantly ladylike with a contemporary edge.

Her legs were left visibly unshaven beneath the abbreviated hemline. Rather than undermining the femininity of the look, unapologetic hair sharpens it. Bridgers’s multiple leg tattoos were also on show, including a tattoo of intertwined thorns and leaves and a black-ink rendering of a house that references her Punisher album.
points: For a turn around the Lido, musician and “Primetime” actor Phoebe Bridgers embraced the glamorous yet free-spirited Venice dress codes her way.

articles.title: Let your mind wander, don’t retire and stop worrying: surprising ways to help save your brain from the cognitive cliff
articles.summary: In his new book, The Brain Cliff, Dr Norman Swan outlines the science of brain ageing and strategies for staving off cognitive decline. You write that “changing the way you think about the brain cliff can literally change the way you think and remember”. How?
body: Dr Norman Swan: There are three things you need to know which are not widely known.

This is about a phenomenon in the brain called scaffolding. To protect our cognitive abilities and perhaps even enhance them as the years pass, our brains build out networks of nerves which act pretty much like the scaffolding inside a skyscraper. It’s the infrastructure around which the brain works. The more successfully we scaffold, the further away we push the brain cliff. This scaffolding initially moves across the brain then into the frontal lobes – the all-important prefrontal cortex which brings our thoughts and memories together and is involved with judgment, decision-making and emotional control.
The third idea is that we should do as much as possible to encourage the scaffolding and as little as possible to get in its way.
You mention that the time to start helping our brains adapt is in our 40s and 50s. What should you be doing at that age and is it ever too late to start?
points: In his new book, The Brain Cliff, Dr Norman Swan outlines the science of brain ageing and strategies for staving off cognitive decline.

articles.title: I slept on a 550lb mattress made of just cotton, wool and coils for a month. Here's the case for old-school beds
articles.summary: This eco-friendly mattress made from organic materials as a nice balance of give and underlying firmness, though it’s pretty bouncy. Sign up for the Filter US newsletter, your weekly guide to buying fewer, better things.
body: Sleep sits at the base of psychologist Abraham Maslow’s famous pyramid of needs, and it’s especially frustrating when a good night’s rest evades your grasp. Personally, thanks to a combination of a bad back and a sleep disorder, it’s all about the right mattress.

For nearly a month, I tested the Naturepedic Serenade, the cheapest mattress from an eco-friendly brand that offers three firmness options: Plush, Cushion-Firm and Firm, all made from cotton and organic materials rather than chemical foams. I tried a queen-sized firm version – I favor a mattress that supports me while sleeping on my back or side. And after a few weeks’ rest, I’m pleased to report that it is a great combination: I got a comfortable night’s sleep with reassuringly firm support and a little bit of give.

I slept on the mattress with my wife, my dog and our two cats for several weeks, keeping notes on how well we (the humans) slept, and using my Apple Watch to track my sleep patterns. We invited others to lay down and test the comfort of the mattress, and I also used weights to simulate different body types using the mattress.
The give: how much you sink into the mattress when you lie on it.
points: This eco-friendly mattress made from organic materials as a nice balance of give and underlying firmness, though it’s pretty bouncy.

articles.title: Ever Anderson Marked Her First Venice Film Festival Premiere in Style
articles.summary: The rising actor and daughter of Milla Jovovich wore Dior and vintage for her first Venice: “I wanted something that was easy to wear but super fun and flashy.”
body: It was an exciting Venice Film Festival for rising actor Ever Anderson this year. The 18-year-old star—and daughter to Milla Jovovich—marked her first turn on the Lido this week with the premiere of her new film, Barthélemy Grossmann’s Father Joe, co-starring Kiefer Sutherland and Al Pacino. (Not a bad way to debut, alongside two such Hollywood heavyweights.) “It was just such an incredible project to work on,” says Anderson of her buzzy role.

The action-thriller film follows a man of faith (Sutherland) engaging in a violent war against Manhattan's criminal underworld; Anderson’s Felicity becomes his unlikely sidekick. “Her empathy and non-judgmental lens toward others was what drew me toward her,” says Anderson, who instantly resonated with the character. “She really felt like a real person when I read the script, which is rare, because normally a character doesn’t feel real on a page until a human plays them—but this wasn’t the case for Felicity. She was so well written that her spirit quite literally jumped off the page.”

articles.title: All the Best Looks From the 2026 Venice Film Festival
articles.summary: As the 2026 Venice Film Festival kicks off this week, all eyes will be on the red carpet—with the likes of George and Amal Clooney, Claire Foy, and Robert Pattinson arriving in the Italian city. See all the best fashion from Venice Film Festival so far.
body: Red carpet lovers, it’s your lucky day: The 2026 Venice Film Festival has officially arrived.

The film roster for this year’s festival has plenty of buzzy projects to take in: Among them is Martin McDonagh’s Oscar-tipped black comedy Wild Horse Nine; Lance Oppenheim’s Primetime; a Robert Pattinson-led portrait of To Catch a Predator host Chris Hansen; and Bunker, Florian Zeller’s marital drama starring Penélope Cruz and Javier Bardem.

Better year, however, is what all of these A-listers will be wearing on the step and repeat for the splashy premieres. This is, after all, the festival that last year offered the first glimpses of new-era Chanel, Dior, Versace and Bottega Veneta before their respective runway debuts, and which has given us Lady Gaga’s feathered Valentino couture gown in 2018 and Zendaya’s wet-look Balmain dress in 2021, among other standout moments.

articles.title: The “Curtain Crop” Is The Cool-Girl Haircut for Fall 2026
articles.summary: Part Kiera Knightley in ‘Bend It Like Beckham,’ part Gina Gershon in ‘Bound,’ part Carrie-Anne Moss in ‘The Matrix,’ the grown-out crop is already this year’s most in-demand style.
body: If you’ve been knocking around the coffee shops, dive bars and small plates restaurants in the cool neighborhoods of New York, Los Angeles, or London recently, you’ll probably have noticed a particular haircut constantly in your periphery. Maybe you already know the one I’m talking about. Maybe you’re even considering succumbing to the style yourself. I’m referring to the curtain crop. The one that’s not dissimilar to the softer, more feminine pixie style we saw a lot of last year, only it’s more grown-out and androgynous, with a floppy middle part or curtains for that added nonchalance.

Think: a mixture of Keira Knightley in Bend It Like Beckham, Gina Gershon in Bound, and Carrie-Anne Moss in The Matrix. It’s essentially a style that’s custom-made for running your fingers through, and looking thoroughly unbothered while doing so (like a young Leo DiCaprio, but for the girls and the theys).
points: Part Kiera Knightley in ‘Bend It Like Beckham,’ part Gina Gershon in ‘Bound,’ part Carrie-Anne Moss in ‘The Matrix,’ the grown-out crop is already this year’s most in-demand style.
